task: Expansion backlog synthesis — master plan for content growth

expansion_backlog_master.total_items_to_process: ~3,300 operations (recalibrations + new content + quality fixes + certifications + metadata updates)
expansion_backlog_master.total_calendar_span: 12 weeks (Sprint 1: 1 wk + Sprint 2: 2 wks + Sprint 3: 3 wks + Sprint 4: 6 wks)
expansion_backlog_master.sequencing_principle: Fix structure → Recalibrate metadata → Fill quality gaps → Create new content → Certify
sequencing_rationale: Structural fixes (DL-016, DL-021) must precede recalibration — recalibrating broken items wastes effort
Recalibration (PH1, DL-031, VDiff bridge) must precede content creation — you cannot author to target distributions if the baseline distribution is wrong
Quality gaps (DL-026, DL-035) are certification-blockers — must be resolved before new content enters the certification pipeline
Content creation (VDiff, Evaluate, Analyze, topic fills) can begin after recalibration establishes the target distribution
Certification is the final gate — all structural, quality, and calibration checks must pass before Certification

items.name: DL-031 coordinated difficulty recalibration sweep (800–1,000 items)
items.dependency: S831-PH1 (Sprint 1) — recalibration methodology validated in Sprint 1; DL-031 is the same operation type at larger scale
items.description: Systematic recalibration of items where the stem contains a textbook definition and the correct answer is the defined term. These items test Bloom's Remember/Understand but are labeled Moderate (3). Change: Difficulty: 'Moderate' → 'Easy', DifficultyScore: 3 → 1. Each item must pass the definition-match check: lexical overlap ≥50% between stem keywords and correct-answer choice text, AND distractors do not require Apply-level discernment.
items.methodology: Phase 1 — Automated scan: regex-based definition-match detection across all 5 packs. Phase 2 — Manual verification: random sample audit (10%) to confirm no false positives. Phase 3 — Batch recalibration: ≤30 items per write, per-pack parallelization.
items.governance_note: Critical path item — DL-031 resolution re-sizes all downstream difficulty distribution targets. The current pool has <5% Easy items; target is 15%. Without DL-031, content authoring targets are wrong (authoring to incorrect baseline).
items.quality_gate: Post-recalibration: Easy band ~15% (target: 15% per CAQS §6.1). Random sample audit: ≥95% accuracy on recalibrated items.

items.methodology: Pack B Section F (50 items) — direct certification (structurally clean). Pack C Section F (74 items) — resolve DL-035 first (author ~117 empty distractor EW slots), then certify. Per-item verification at HIGH confidence across all six dimensions.
items.governance_note: DL-035 items must not be certified with empty non-CC EW slots (governance guard Rule 6 BLOCK). Certification = question_state: 'Certified' — triggers learner-pool inclusion. REVISION_HISTORY entry per certification wave.

These items currently exist but are labeled Moderate or Difficult. Recalibrate: Difficulty: → 'Very Difficult', DifficultyScore: → 5.

items.quality_gate: Independent verification: 22/22 items pass DifficultyScore: 5 audit (tested against CAQS §6.1 criteria)

Topics: master budget reconciliation, flexible budget variance chains, transfer pricing with capacity constraints, ROI vs. RI comparison with multiple adjustments.

items.description: Author 40 new Evaluate-level items targeting Sections E (Internal Controls) and F (Technology and Analytics). Evaluate = professional judgment: assess control environment, recommend risk responses, evaluate system implementation alternatives recommend cybersecurity posture, assess data governance maturity. No defined-formula items — judgment-based with scenario context.
items.methodology: 0.4 hours/item. 2 batches of 20 items. Two-phase authoring: Phase 1 — write scenario and stem (0.2h), Phase 2 — craft distractors and explanations (0.2h). Each item scenario must include: named company, stakeholder role, business trigger, decision context.
items.governance_note: Evaluate items are the hardest to author correctly. Risk: items may collapse to 'Analyze' level without realizing it. Mitigation: independent Bloom's audit on 100% of Evaluate items before certification.

items.description: Author 100 new Analyze-level items across Sections D (Cost Management), E (Internal Controls), and F (Technology and Analytics). Analyze = interpret data, identify patterns, compare alternatives. Topics: variance analysis interpretation, cost behavior pattern identification, control deficiency classification, data trend interpretation, ERP module integration analysis.
items.methodology: 0.4 hours/item. 4 batches of 25 items across 4 packs. Section D (25): cost drivers, CVP multi-product, relevant cost scenarios. Section E (25): control deficiency severity, COSO component assessment, fraud risk factor analysis. Section F (50): data visualization selection, system integration analysis, analytics tool appropriateness.
items.governance_note: This is the largest single content creation batch in the S833 plan. Risk: quality dilution at volume. Mitigation: per-batch quality gates — batch N+1 cannot start until batch N passes audit.

items.name: Case difficulty calibration (330 items, scored_cases2–5)
items.dependency: None technically — case files are independent of MCQ pack files and can be calibrated in parallel with other Sprint 3 items
items.description: All 330 case items across 55 cases (scored_cases2–5) are labeled 'Moderate' with zero variance. Recalibrate to CAQS §6.1 target distribution: Easy ~15%, Moderate-Easy ~20%, Moderate ~30%, Difficult ~25%, VDiff ~10%. Calibration criteria: (1) position in case (items 1-2 Easier, items 5-6 Harder), (2) cognitive level, (3) calculation complexity, (4) number of exhibits referenced.
items.methodology: Case-by-case calibration. Items 1-2 per case → Easy to Moderate-Easy (foundational calculation/recall). Items 3-4 → Moderate to Difficult (analysis/interpretation). Items 5-6 → Difficult to VDiff (judgment/synthesis). Batch: 4 batches of ~15 cases. Batch-cap adjustment: scored_cases files use case-level objects (5-6 items per case), so 15 cases = ~80 items = within 30-item governance limit per individual item write.
items.governance_note: Case item calibration does not change content — only Difficulty and DifficultyScore fields. No ExplanationWrong, CorrectChoice, or Stem modifications. REVISION_HISTORY entry per case file.
items.quality_gate: Post-calibration: 0 items labeled 'Moderate' that should be in another tier. Case difficulty progression maintained (items 1-2 easier than items 5-6).

items.dependency: S833-DL032 (Sprint 3) — case difficulty must be calibrated before certification. DL-023 (exhibit headers) must be resolved for scored_cases3/4/5 (17 exhibits, 9 cases) — resolved 2026-07-23.
items.description: Certify all 300 case items across 50 cases. Six-dimension CAQS verification per case: (1) accounting correctness, (2) precision, (3) difficulty calibration, (4) distractor engineering, (5) blueprint alignment, (6) CMA Part 1 relevance. Each case must pass: cognitive progression (items 1-6 progress from Apply → Evaluate), exhibit data consumption (all exhibit data referenced by ≥1 item), independent answerability (no item requires correct answer to prior item).
items.methodology: 50 cases × 0.8 hours/case = 40 hours. Per-case verification: solve all items independently, verify exhibit data consistency, audit cognitive progression, confirm blueprint alignment. Cases with defects are routed to Editorial Queue; clean cases transition to Certified.
items.governance_note: Case certification is the longest pole in Sprint 4. Start earliest. If resources constrained, prioritize cases in Sections E and F (highest Bloom's calibration need).

risk_register.risk: Recalibration without per-item review may mislabel items (DL-031 pattern: definition-match items incorrectly classified as Easy)
risk_register.impact: ~50-100 items wrongly calibrated — requires re-remediation pass, pushes schedule by 1 week
risk_register.trigger: Post-recalibration audit finds >5% error rate in sample
risk_register.mitigation: Sample audit 10% of recalibrated items per batch. Publish QID lists for independent verification. Halt recalibration if error rate >5%.
risk_register.contingency: Revert from backup, refine detection rule, re-execute

risk_register.risk: Content authoring pipeline not yet established for 740 new items — quality may degrade at volume
risk_register.impact: New items require re-authoring or extensive revision; delays content expansion by 4-6 weeks
risk_register.trigger: Pilot batch audit finds <70% of items pass CAQS at ≥HIGH confidence
risk_register.mitigation: Start with pilot batch of 25 items (5 per type). Establish authoring templates, review checklists, QA pipeline before scaling. Require independent verification for all new items. Do not proceed to Sprint 3 authoring until pilot passes.
risk_register.contingency: Reduce scope (fewer new items). Focus on quality over quantity. Extend Sprint 4 timeline.

risk_register.risk: Governance guard batch limits (≤30 items per write) constrain throughput — 300+ batches needed for full plan
risk_register.impact: ~75 hours of batch overhead across full plan. May extend calendar time if batches must be serial.
risk_register.trigger: Per-batch REVISION_HISTORY entry, backup, write, verify cycle takes >25 minutes average
risk_register.mitigation: Automate REVISION_HISTORY generation. Parallelize batches where packs differ. Pre-compute batch QID lists. Use task agents for per-batch execution.
risk_register.contingency: Request BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker for high-confidence mechanical operations (recalibration, not content authoring)

risk_register.risk: Certified item changes require REVISION_HISTORY entries for all ~2,000+ operations
risk_register.impact: Manual REVISION_HISTORY entry overhead unsustainable at scale
risk_register.trigger: REVISION_HISTORY.md grows by >500 lines per sprint (manual writing bottleneck)
risk_register.mitigation: Automate REVISION_HISTORY generation. Batch-level entries (one entry per batch) rather than per-item entries for recalibration operations. Reserve per-item entries for content changes (answer, explanation, distractor).
risk_register.contingency: Use session-summary entries that list QID ranges and operation types

risk_register.risk: Pack A/B/C write conflicts in Sprint 4 parallel execution (EVAL2 + ANALYZE2 + VDIFF3 all touch Pack A/B/C)
risk_register.impact: DL-019 concurrent-write data loss — one agent's work silently overwrites another's
risk_register.trigger: Two agents write to the same pack file within the same calendar day
risk_register.mitigation: Per-pack write sequencing: each pack has a single owner agent per calendar day. Section-level assignment: VDIFF3 = Pack A Sections A/D, ANALYZE2 = Pack A Sections B/C, EVAL2 = Pack A Sections empty. Or: sequential execution — one workstream completes Pack A before next starts.
risk_register.contingency: Immediate halt, restore from backup, re-execute lost writes. Implement file-lock protocol.

risk_register.risk: DL-035 (39 Certified Domain F items with empty EW slots) blocks Section F certification
risk_register.impact: Section F certification (S833-SECF, Sprint 2) cannot proceed until DL-035 is resolved
risk_register.trigger: Governance guard Rule 6 BLOCKs certification attempt on items with empty non-CC EW slots
risk_register.mitigation: Resolve DL-035 in Sprint 1 or early Sprint 2 (author ~117 distractor EW fields for 39 items). This is a prerequisite for S833-SECF.
risk_register.contingency: Certify Pack B Section F first (0 DL-035). Certify Pack C Section F after DL-035 remediation.

risk_register.risk: Baseline drift between sprints — recalibration in Sprint 1 changes counts that Sprint 2-4 plans depend on
risk_register.impact: Content authoring targets are wrong because the baseline moved post-recalibration
risk_register.trigger: Post-Baseline.5 certified count differs from pre-Baseline.4 by >50 items
risk_register.mitigation: Re-run CURRENT_BASELINES.md update after each sprint. Compare certified counts, difficulty distribution, and Bloom's distribution against Sprint N targets. Adjust Sprint N+1 targets if baseline drifts.
risk_register.contingency: Flexible scope: if actual numbers are lower, reduce authoring volume. If higher, accelerate.

risk_register.risk: Case certification (S833-CASE) requires accounting expertise for 50 cases across 6 domains — single-agent bottleneck
risk_register.impact: Case certification extends beyond Sprint 4 (6 weeks → 8-10 weeks)
risk_register.trigger: Case certification velocity <10 cases per week
risk_register.mitigation: Start case certification in Sprint 3 (not Sprint 4). Parallelize: assign different agents to different case files. Pre-certify structurally clean cases first.
risk_register.contingency: Reduce case certification scope: certify Sections E/F cases first (highest need), defer Sections A-D cases.

governance_compliance.rule1_question_state_changes: Every question_state change (RECALIBRATE operations modify Difficulty/DifficultyScore — these are metadata changes, not question_state changes. CERTIFY operations change question_state and require paired REVISION_HISTORY entries.
governance_compliance.rule2_dl008_block: All AUTHOR operations must verify ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] is empty after authoring. Governance guard Rule 2 BLOCK applies to all pack-file writes.
governance_compliance.rule3_registry_no_hand_edit: MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md must be regenerated after each sprint — no manual edits.
governance_compliance.rule5_batch_cap: ≤30 items per write operation. Recalibration: 423 items = 15 batches. DL-031: 800-1000 items = 28-34 batches. New content: ≤30 items per batch. Request BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker for mechanical recalibration operations to lift batch cap.
governance_compliance.rule6_dl026_block: Active as of S814. All CERTIFY operations must verify 0 empty non-CC EW slots. This is enforced by governance guard pre-write gate.
governance_compliance.backup_protocol: Mandatory timestamped backup before every pack-file write. Expected ~100 backup files generated across 4 sprints.

end_of_sprint_3.Content pipeline maturity: ≥90% new items pass CAQS at HIGH confidence

end_of_sprint_4.Blueprint coverage: All 6 domains with ≥100 certified items each

decision.rationale: The expansion backlog addresses all 19 gaps from the S832 Gap Register (8 Content, 6 Quality, 5 Calibration) in priority order: structural fixes first, then recalibration, then quality, then content creation, then certification. The critical path is well-understood. Risks are identified with mitigations. Parallelization opportunities exist to compress calendar time. The 12-week timeline is achievable with dedicated resources.
decision.immediate_next_action: Begin Sprint 1 immediately — execute S831-PH1 (calibration), S833-DL021 (Pack E), S833-DL016 (Pack A Section E) in parallel. Sprint 2-4 decisions are pending Sprint 1 completion and baseline re-measurement.
decision.blockers: None for Sprint 1. Sprint 2 blocker: DL-035 resolution must precede Section F certification (39 items, ~117 EW fields). Sprint 3-4 blockers: content authoring pipeline must be validated before scaling.
decision.escalation_required: Request BLOCK-AUTHORIZED marker for mechanical recalibration operations (S831-PH1, S831-DL031) to lift the 30-item batch cap for operations that do not modify content (only metadata fields: Difficulty, DifficultyScore).
decision.governance_signoff: Pending user review and acceptance of the expansion backlog. RECOMMENDED: review Sprint 1-2 scope for immediate execution; defer Sprint 3-4 scope decisions until Sprint 1 baseline is stable.
